content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained or delayed price corrections.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overreacts to recent spikes, then underreacts to subsequent drops.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 38.18 or 36.84) by 5–10% and fails to adjust downward in the following days.
- Underestimates low-price periods (e.g., 31–33 range) and overestimates mid-range values (34–36) — exhibits asymmetric bias toward higher prices.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true price movements often occur 2–5 days after model’s peak or trough.
- Model fails to capture sudden policy or market shocks — e.g., abrupt drops after spikes (e.g., 38.18 → 33.77) are not reflected in forecast decay.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to account for volatility clustering or sudden reversals in price direction.
